provenance: Computed by the LunarWindow pipeline from NASA LOLA terrain and NASA SPICE (DE421) ephemerides. Code written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and verified by the team with automated tests and a comparison against NASA PGDA illumination maps.
verdict: Touchdown 2028-10-24T06 UTC: the Sun's centre is 2.25 deg above the skyline and the top of Earth's disc 0.00 deg above the skyline (power and a link at landing).
Over 14 days: Sun up 100%, Earth in view 96%, both 96% of the time.
Survives the mission: the battery never drops below 140 Wh (lowest 700 Wh).
No darkness during the mission: no cold soak.
Battery used on this mission: 0 Wh of the 560 Wh it can use above its 140 Wh floor.
Battery model: power = panel power x visible Sun, whatever the Sun's direction (a sun-tracking array), so survival is an upper bound for fixed panels.
why: Marginal touchdown: the top of Earth's disc clears the skyline by under 0.5 deg; Earth is 0.00 deg above the skyline (bearing 170 deg, set by the Moon's own curvature at -1.24 deg), so there is almost no margin for a landing error, a lower antenna or a later hour.
Longest Earth blackout from 2028-11-06T18 UTC (12 h): it is below the Moon's own curvature (bearing 157 deg, horizon -0.37 deg).
The Sun stays up all mission: its closest pass, 2028-11-01T23 UTC, is 0.98 deg above the skyline (bearing 165 deg, set by terrain 2.9 km away at 0.19 deg).
